newsitem.title: UK: Amnesty says human rights top Zaire priority.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty says human rights top Zaire priority.

text.p: Amnesty International said on Thursday human rights should be a top priority for the multinational force being sent to Zaire.
The human rights pressure group said genocide suspects should be arrested, combatants excluded from refugee camps and refugees only returned home if they really wanted to go.

In a statement aimed at the U.N. Security Council, Amnesty said: "The only way that the international force can make a real impact on this crisis is by tackling both the human rights and humanitarian problems."

It cited a string of more than 1,500 alleged human rights violations in the Great Lakes countries and said, "The international forces should not acquiesce or participate in any repatriation that is not completely voluntary."

The U.N. envoy negotiating a mandate for the force with Rwanda and Zaire, whose army is battling Rwandan-backed Tutsi rebels, has said it was unclear how the Canadian-led troops could handle armed Hutus using refugees as a screen.
Most are former soldiers of the Rwanda armed forces who fled with Hutu civilians after losing a civil war following the 1994 massacre of Tutsis in Rwanda.
